name: Red Tracton's Steakhouse
notes: Router said no-platform on the homepage/menus page (both of which are genuinely empty of prices - the /menus/ landing page carries only a 'Dinner Menu' heading with no content below it). The actual priced menus live at separate WordPress pages not linked from primary nav, found via /wp-json/wp/v2/pages/: /dinner/ (79 prices) and /lunch/ (33 prices), both first-party, structured HTML (av-catalogue-title/price/content markup). Own-site tier-1 source; no markup test needed (not a delivery/ordering platform). Price level is plausible for a 2026 high-end steakhouse (prime rib $50-80, filet $52-94, sandwiches $30-43). 6 items with only a range in the visible price field (e.g. 'Our Famous Jumbo Shrimp $40/$60 (4) or (6)') were split into one dish per confirmed size/count using the size labels printed in each item's own description text - nothing was divided or averaged, each figure is a distinct price actually printed on the page. 2 dinner items (Prime Rib, Filet Mignon Bearnaise) print their per-size prices only inside the description text rather than the price field ('8 oz $50 / 14 oz $65 / Bone-In 24 oz $80') and were split the same way. Sections reached - Dinner: Appetizers, Soups & Salads, Charbroiled Beef & Chops, Fish & Seafood, Red's Q, Red's Favorite's, Sandwiches, Small Sides, Premium Sides (Specials list has no prices, excluded). Lunch: Appetizers & Soups, Salads, Sandwiches, Seafood, Red's Favorites, Breakfast. This reads as the complete dinner and lunch menu.

name: Hilberto's Mexican Food
blocked: only a breakfast-items slice is priced anywhere reachable; tacos, burritos, plates, tostadas, tortas and enchiladas - the bulk of the menu - have no priced source
notes: No website on record. hilbertos.com (found via web search) no longer resolves (DNS failure, confirmed with curl -v) - domain is dead. Its Wayback Machine snapshot from 2024-12-04 (http://web.archive.org/web/20241204100924/http://www.hilbertos.com/menu/) shows a full first-party item list - Breakfast Burritos, Special Breakfast Plates, Burritos, Tacos, Combination Plates, Special Plates, Rolled Tacos, Tostadas, Tortas, Enchiladas, Side Orders, Extras, Drinks, numbered Specials - but the page prints ZERO prices for any item, own site or archived. SinglePlatform (places.singleplatform.com/hilbertos-mexican-food-4/menu, address matches exactly) carries prices but only for the Breakfast Burritos/Combos/Tortas/TJ Street Tacos sections - 12 items, $2.95-$9.50 - and is silent on every other section the restaurant's own site lists (Burritos, Tacos, Combination Plates, Tostadas, Enchiladas etc.), so it is a partial in the same way a single daypart capture is: what's there reads like a fraction of the true menu, not the whole thing. Per playbook this is treated as blocked rather than filed as a partial. No DoorDash/Uber Eats/Postmates storefront found for this National City location (a Glendale, AZ location of the same name exists on DoorDash - different restaurant, not used). Yelp 403'd curl (bot wall) before a dated menu photo could be checked. Nothing constructed, divided, or merged. Would need either a Yelp/Google photo of the full priced menu or a working delivery storefront for the non-breakfast sections.

name: Mi Ranchito Taco Shop
blocked: only reachable priced source (DoorDash) fails the 2026 price-level check - implausibly cheap, likely a years-stale snapshot
notes: Router's listed website (Facebook) 400s to curl as noted; found a DoorDash marketplace page instead: https://www.doordash.com/en/store/mi-ranchito-taco-shop-ramona-29648214/37351149/ (address 1028 Main St, Ramona matches). Extracted 53 items from its schema.org Menu JSON-LD via probe/extract_dd_jsonld.js - torta $5.45-$6.95, cheeseburger $4.85, nachos $5.05, flan $1.15, hot sauce $1.50, cheese 3oz $1.95. This price level is implausible for 2026 (rule 6) - reads like a decade-old snapshot never refreshed on the storefront. Confirmed it isn't just a stale JSON-LD block out of sync with a fresher hydrated page: fetched the same store via page-service.doordash.com/store/... (the alternate host noted for 403s) and every dollar-figure in that full page also falls in the same $1.15-$9.70 band - the whole captured page is stale, not just one script tag. Also missing core sections entirely (no Tacos, Burritos, or Combo Plates categories at all, despite those being this restaurant's defining items per other web listings) - both a price-level failure and a section-completeness failure. A WebSearch summary surfaced higher, plausible-sounding figures ($8.99 Nachos, $18.99 Carne Asada Nachos, $11.99 Large Carne Asada Crazy Fries) attributed loosely to 'the menu', but no page actually fetched (DoorDash, page-service mirror, or myorangecrate.com) contained those literal figures anywhere in raw HTML - myorangecrate.com's order page is gated behind an address/login flow with no menu content before that gate, and per rule 13 no personal data was entered to get past it. zmenu and gotoeat.net are barred aggregator/farm domains and were not used. Nothing filed from the DoorDash data since it cannot be trusted as current; needs either a browser session on myorangecrate/DoorDash's live rendered price or a dine-in artefact.

name: Jaquin Mexican Grill
notes: Router's own site (jaquinmexgrill.com) is a bare Homestead/GoDaddy website-builder JS app shell with no static content - confirmed no-platform. Found the restaurant's DoorDash marketplace page instead (address 5102 1/2 Imperial Ave, San Diego confirmed in the page's own text). Extracted 91 items from its schema.org Menu JSON-LD (probe/extract_dd_jsonld.js). Markup test: cent distribution is scattered across 16+ distinct endings (.00 .20 .25 .29 .40 .45 .49 .50 .69 .75 .79 .80 .89 .90 .95 .99, no two-value cluster), and no divisor (1.04-1.30, 0.96) clears more than 19% of items (1.20 got 17/91) - passes, reads as organic POS pricing, not a fee. Price level is plausible for a 2026 no-frills San Diego taco shop (soft tacos $3.49, burritos $5.99-$9.20, quesadillas $4.49-$8.29). DoorDash is a tier-3 white-label marketplace with no independent own-site menu to cross-check, so confidence is capped at medium. One item, '16. Chorizo Con Huevos' priced at $58.99 in the same JSON-LD block, was dropped as an implausible outlier (a combo breakfast plate at 6-10x every neighboring price) rather than guessed or corrected - nothing constructed. Sections reached: Breakfast Special, Soups, Green Salads, Burger, Quesadillas, Crispy Tacos, Soft Tacos, Burritos, Enchiladas, Jaquin's Special's, Combo Plates - this reads as the restaurant's full menu.

name: FRUTAS 3rd Ave.
notes: Router's own site (frutas100natural.com) returns a fatal WordPress 'critical error' page (confirmed on retry, both https 500 and http 406) - genuinely down, not usable. This brand runs three Chula-Vista-area Uber Eats storefronts (Palomar, Broadway, Bonita); checked each one's own escaped address field and only 'Frutas 100% Natural - Palomar Chula Vista' matches the work list's 1329 3rd Ave exactly (Broadway = 616 Broadway, Bonita = 4232 Bonita Rd - both different addresses, not used). Extracted 68 items from that store's __REACT_QUERY_STATE__ blob, which embeds a schema.org Menu (hasMenuSection/MenuItem) doubly escaped (\uXXXX then %5C-for-backslash-quote) - wrote a one-off decoder (not node -e) to normalize both escape layers before regexing MenuItem objects out; verified against the rendered numbers, not guessed. Markup test: cents are irregular and never land on .00/.25/.50/.75/.95/.99 as a printed menu would (.44 .98 .41 .90 .06 .72 .38 etc, 18 distinct endings on 68 items) - not a clean menu, but also not a clean fee: no divisor 1.04-1.30 clears more than 3/68, and the best fit in a full 1.00-1.60 sweep (1.07) only clears 22/68 (32%), well short of 'substantially'. So it fails the printed-menu look-and-feel but doesn't isolate to a removable markup either; recorded as-is at medium confidence, one step down from a clean own-site capture, and flagged rather than silently trusted. Price level (tortas $14.44-$14.98, burritos $10.41-$14.98, coffee $6.38-$7.45, sodas $3.72) is plausible for a 2026 Chula Vista fresh-fruit/torta shop and matches an independent WebSearch summary of the same store's figures almost exactly. No independent own-site or second-owner priced source exists to cross-check (site is down), so this is filed alone. Sections reached: Torta/Sandwich/Wrap & More, Specialty Torta/Sandwich/Wrap & More, Burritos, Breakfast, Fruits & Snacks, Salads, Soups, Smoothies or Licuados, The Best Healthy Juices, Fruit Waters, Other Drinks, Coffee - reads as the complete menu. Nothing divided, merged, or invented; source spells some items 'jalapeńo' (missing tilde) as printed in Uber's own data, left as-is.

name: Konnichiwa Sushi & Bar
notes: No website on record. This restaurant's res-menu.net listing (konnichiwa-sushi-bar.res-menu.net) is behind a Cloudflare challenge page (Cf-Mitigated: challenge) and unreadable by curl; allmenus.com is a barred aggregator with no second independent source to cross-check it against. Found the Uber Eats storefront instead (address 8350 La Mesa Blvd confirmed in the page's own escaped address field) - a WebSearch summary claimed this store was 'closed on Uber Eats as of Jul 24, 2023', but the fetched page's own isOrderable flag reads true and it returned a full, populated catalog, so that claim is stale/wrong. This store carries no schema.org Menu JSON-LD (unlike the DoorDash/other Uber Eats stores read elsewhere this batch) - the menu instead lives in Uber's native catalogSectionsMap/catalogItems structure, each item's price given as labelPrimary.accessibilityText (e.g. '$14.00'). Wrote a new extractor (extract_ubereats3.js) for this structure since none of the existing probe scripts covered it. 136 items across 15 sections. Our menu is under update' - confirmed no-platform. Found the restaurant's own Toast storefront instead (toasttab.com/local/order/the-cup-coffee-206-wisconsin-ave redirects to order.toasttab.com/online/the-cup-coffee-206-wisconsin-ave); the bare www.toasttab.com URL 403'd but the /v3 order link worked with a desktop Chrome UA. Extracted via the rendered HTML item markup (headerText/priceLine spans), reusing probe/extract_toast3.js's approach; that script's price regex assumes a clean '$X.XX' close and silently drops 6 items whose price is followed by an HTML comment plus a '+' (Toast's 'starting from' notation for size-variable drinks, rendered as '$2.00+'), so I patched the regex to also capture that suffix - recovered Coffee, Americano, Cappuccino, Latte, Chai Latte and Hot Chocolate, which the unpatched script would have dropped entirely. Those 6 are recorded at their printed starting price with a note that larger sizes cost more (not derived - it's the exact figure printed on the page). 72 items total across Sandwiches, Pastries, Drinks, Retail, Front Fridge and a small ROLLS (sushi) section that appears to be a shared-kitchen offering on the same storefront - included as-is since it's part of this Toast catalog. Prices are clean whole/half-dollar or .50 values with no scattered-cents markup pattern; own-platform tier-1 source. Retail items (mugs, t-shirts, stickers) are adjuncts but were left in since they're on the same priced catalog and small in number - flagged here rather than silently included. This reads as the complete menu.
